title: Tensor product of a geometrically normal algebra and a normal algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $A$ and $B$ be commutative $k$-algebras. Assume $A$ is geometrically normal over $k$, meaning that for every field extension $E/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] the commutative tensor-product algebra $A\otimes_k E$ is a normal ring. Assume $B$ is a normal ring [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Then $A\otimes_k B$ is a normal ring: each of its prime localizations is an integrally closed domain. Tensor products are commutative tensor-product algebras [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with $(a\otimes b)(a^{\prime}\otimes b^{\prime})=aa^{\prime}\otimes bb^{\prime}$ and unit $1\otimes1$. No Noetherian, finite-type, domain or nonzero hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.
